chunks.text: Gamescom, the world's largest [[trade fair]] for video games, {{wrapped up}} in Cologne, Germany, on Sunday, August 30. Organizers said 368,000 visitors from 131 countries {{turned out}} over the week, up from 357,000 in 2025. The number of international visitors hit a record, and 72 percent of the 1,743 [[exhibitors]] came from outside Germany, another record. For the first time, all 233,000 square meters of [[floor space]] {{sold out}}.

verbs.correct: To bring an event to an end
verbs.wrong: To move an event to a later date
verbs.why: A teacher wraps up the lesson five minutes early on Fridays. Our team wraps up every meeting with a short vote. Gamescom wrapped up in Cologne on Sunday, August 30, after a week of games.

verbs.correct: To attend an event in large numbers
verbs.wrong: To be refused entry at the door
verbs.why: Thousands of fans turn out for the city's parade every year. Only a few neighbors turn out for town meetings. Some 368,000 visitors from 131 countries turned out for Gamescom this year.

verbs.correct: To be all sold with none left
verbs.wrong: To be offered at a lower price
verbs.why: Concert tickets for big stars sell out in an hour. A popular new phone often sells out on its first day. All 233,000 square meters of floor space at Gamescom sold out for the first time.

chunks.text: Gamescom is a giant [[showcase]] where game companies {{show off}} titles that are not [[on sale]] yet. The week {{kicks off}} with Opening Night Live, a two-hour show of new [[trailers]] streamed around the world. This year it {{drew in}} 78 million views. Business days for the [[games industry]] come next. Then the [[halls]] open to the public, and fans wait in [[long lines]] to play games months before their [[release]].

verbs.wrong: To arrive at a place as planned
verbs.why: Kids show off their new bikes to the whole street. A chef shows off three new dishes at a restaurant opening. At Gamescom, game companies show off titles that are not on sale yet.
The festival kicks off with fireworks on Friday. Our season kicks off next week with a home game. Gamescom kicks off with Opening Night Live, a two-hour show of new trailers.
A new museum draws in thousands of visitors every month. A good trailer draws in players before the game exists. Opening Night Live drew in 78 million views this year.

chunks.text: Opening Night Live {{lined up}} 55 games, and more than half came from China, South Korea, and Japan. The biggest [[announcement]] was a [[remastered]] version of The Witcher 3, a free [[upgrade]] for current owners that arrives on September 29. A full 3D [[remake]] of Heroes of Might and Magic III was also {{rolled out}}, with a 2027 release date. By Saturday evening, Gamescom content had {{racked up}} more than 624 million views online.

verbs.correct: To arrange for something to happen
verbs.wrong: To cut a show short at the end
verbs.why: A school lines up three speakers for its graduation event. A good manager lines up interviews for the whole week. Opening Night Live lined up 55 games, more than half of them from Asia.

verbs.correct: To present something new to the public
verbs.wrong: To fall behind a planned schedule
verbs.why: Banks roll out new apps every year. Many cities roll out electric buses on busy routes. A full 3D remake of Heroes of Might and Magic III was rolled out at the show.

verbs.correct: To collect a large number gradually
verbs.wrong: To divide a total into equal parts
verbs.why: A funny video racks up a million views in a day. A good player racks up points all season long. Gamescom content had racked up more than 624 million views by Saturday evening.

chunks.text: More than 36,000 [[trade visitors]] attended, about half of them from abroad. Some 6,200 people {{signed up}} for the [[developer conference]], up 15 percent. Germany's federal president also {{stopped by}} the Gamescom congress for the first time. A [[city festival]] in [[downtown]] Cologne attracted about 80,000 people. Organizers say the figures {{back up}} Gamescom's role as the central [[platform]] for the international games industry. Gamescom 2027 is set for August 23 to 29.

verbs.correct: To put your name on a list to join
verbs.why: Many adults sign up for a Spanish class in January. Hundreds of runners sign up for the city race each spring. Some 6,200 people signed up for the developer conference at Gamescom.
My aunt stops by for coffee every Sunday morning. Parents stop by the new library on opening day. Germany's federal president stopped by the Gamescom congress for the first time.

verbs.correct: To give support to a claim
verbs.wrong: To repeat a claim many times
verbs.why: The photos back up his story about the storm. Sales numbers back up the manager's plan. Organizers say the visitor figures back up Gamescom's role as the industry's central platform.

mainIdea.s: Gamescom closed in Cologne with 368,000 visitors and a record share of foreign exhibitors. Organizers say the numbers confirm the fair's central place in the global games business.
mainIdea.why: Visitors came from 131 countries, 72 percent of exhibitors were foreign, and organizers say the figures back up Gamescom's role as the industry's central platform.

mainIdea.s: The Cologne games fair ended with 368,000 visitors, but exhibitor numbers fell and some halls stayed half empty. Organizers hope more foreign companies will come back to the fair in 2027.
mainIdea.why: Close, but exhibitors rose 11 percent to 1,743, and for the first time all 233,000 square meters of floor space sold out.

mainIdea.s: A new video game fair in Cologne is trying to compete with older shows in Los Angeles and Tokyo. Its first edition drew 36,000 visitors, and organizers hope to reach 100,000 by 2027.
mainIdea.why: Gamescom is not new and already draws hundreds of thousands. The 36,000 figure is the number of trade visitors, not the total attendance.

lines.text: Gamescom {{wrapped up}} in Cologne on Sunday. 368,000 visitors from 131 countries.
Gamescom? I've never heard of it. What is it exactly?
It's the world's largest trade fair for video games. Companies {{show off}} titles that aren't on sale yet, and fans get to play them first.
So it's like a movie festival, but for games.
Pretty close. The week {{kicks off}} with Opening Night Live, a two-hour show of new trailers. It {{drew in}} 78 million views this year.
78 million? For trailers? [[Now I get it]]. That's why the companies spend so much money there.
Right. The show {{lined up}} 55 games, and more than half came from China, South Korea, and Japan.
Anything big? I only play a few games a year.
A remastered version of The Witcher 3, free for current owners. It arrives on September 29. And a full 3D remake of Heroes of Might and Magic III for 2027.
Free? [[That's the appeal]] for me. I still have the old game. So who actually goes to Cologne?
First there are business days for the games industry. More than 36,000 trade visitors {{turned out}}, half of them from abroad. Then the halls open to the public.
And people wait in line for hours to play a game they could buy in a few months? [[Not my thing]].
Fans love it. All 233,000 square meters of floor space {{sold out}}, and 72 percent of the exhibitors came from outside Germany.
That is a lot of space. Did anyone important go?
Germany's federal president {{stopped by}} the congress for the first time. And 6,200 people {{signed up}} for the developer conference.
Okay, [[worth the trip]] then. Do those numbers really {{back up}} the idea that Cologne is the center of the games business?
The organizers think so. Online, the content {{racked up}} more than 624 million views by Saturday. The next one is set for August 23 to 29, 2027.
[[Put it on the calendar]]. I'd fly there just for the free remaster news.
